headline: Congress Swears In Hottest Freshman Class Since the Whig Party's 1848 Intake
subheadline: *Exit polls confirm 'the jawline' now outranks the economy, healthcare and literally everything else as the decisive issue of our time.*
author: Clementine Vane-Whitlock, Internet Culture Desk
seoTitle: Congress Swears In Hottest Freshman Class in History
seoDescription: Satire: Democrats' midterm sweep produces a congressional freshman class so photogenic that democracy has officially merged with Instagram's explore page.
sourceEvent: Following major Democratic victories in the 2026 US midterm elections, social media filled with celebratory 'thirst trap' posts about attractive newly elected male candidates. NPR reported the viral trend is bigger than a meme, reflecting the shifting politics of masculinity in the age of Trump.

altHeadlines: C-SPAN Ratings Quadruple After Nation Discovers Committee Hearings Feature Jawlines
Exit Polls Add 'Can He Get It' Category After Write-Ins Overwhelm Volunteers

body:
WASHINGTON — Americans went to the polls this week to determine the direction of the republic, and have unanimously concluded that the direction is "towards the soft-focus lens, possibly the one with the ring light".

Within hours of the midterm results being called, the nation's political discourse — historically a marketplace of ideas — completed its transition into a marketplace of jawlines, as millions of voters celebrated the incoming Democratic freshman class in the traditional manner: slow-motion fancams set to music that would make a founding father file a restraining order.

Exit poll data confirmed the shift. "The economy" placed a distant third behind "protecting democracy" and "can he get it", a category pollsters added this cycle after respondents refused to stop writing it in.

"We used to ask voters about kitchen-table issues," said Dr Lenora Figg, senior fellow at the Centre for Electoral Behaviour. "Now the kitchen-table issue is whether a candidate can lean against one while holding a mug."

The consequences arrived quickly. Congressional orientation week, previously a fortnight of ethics briefings, now includes a mandatory ring-light tutorial and a session titled "Governing for the Front Camera". Official portraits will be shot by the photographer who does the perfume adverts. C-SPAN viewership is up 4,000 per cent, with C-SPAN3 — a channel previously believed to be theoretical — now a round-the-clock livestream of one freshman representative reading an appropriations bill.

A spokesperson for the House confirmed that an incoming member, internally codenamed "Mr November", had been formally reminded that the Congressional Record does not accept submissions in the form of lip-sync videos.

Voters insist the phenomenon is substantive. "I voted on policy," said local man Gerald Pruitt, 54. "Then I saw the clip of him taking his jacket off before a town hall, and now I have watched it forty times. For policy."

Political analysts agree the trend is bigger than a meme, noting it says something profound about masculinity in the modern era, though none has managed to finish the sentence because they keep scrolling.

Strategists on both sides are already adapting. Recruitment teams have reportedly begun scouting gyms, independent bookshops and "that one farmers' market everyone pretends not to go to", while a leading think tank published a 40-page paper titled *Thirst as Constituency: Measuring the Smoulder-to-Substance Ratio*. Constitutional scholars note that the Framers did technically invent the calendar, so this outcome was always available.

The Library of Congress has begun quietly reclassifying representative democracy under "lifestyle content", and several senators have enquired whether the filibuster can be performed in portrait orientation.

At press time, Congress's approval rating had climbed to an unprecedented "would".
